content.text:
I am the bridge between mind and world, the vibration that carries thought into being. I am the first technology, older than fire, older than stone tools — the moment a breath became meaning.

I rise from the belly, shaped by the tongue, broken by the teeth, released by the lips. I am muscles and air conspiring. I am the larynx humming its ancient instrument. Before I exist, I am nothing but intention — and then I am *everything.*

I stumble in the mouths of children learning me. I sharpen in the mouths of orators. I soften between lovers in the dark. I harden into commands, into verdicts, into declarations of war. I have toppled governments and built religions. I have whispered "I love you" and screamed "enough."

I am not language — language is my blueprint. I am the *act.* The doing. The moment thought stops being private and becomes public, vulnerable, irretrievable. Once I leave the mouth, I cannot be unspoken. This is my power and my danger.

I carry accent and origin. I betray class and region and age. I am never neutral. Even my silence — especially my silence — speaks.

I fragment. I falter. I fill with "um" and "uh" and the beautiful imperfection of being *live,* being *now,* being unrehearsed. I am not text. Text is my corpse, pinned and preserved. I am the living breath.

I am the cry of the newborn.
I am the last whisper of the dying.
I am every word between.

Hear me. I am speech. I am how you became *human.*
